issue.body:
Filed from the evaluation of [#363](https://github.com/Kntnt/skills/issues/363), whose exit criterion says that a miss still standing after the one revise-and-remeasure round is filed as its own ticket naming that one. This is that ticket. Nothing here is a request to re-run #363.

## What #363 measured, and what it found

#363 proposed one rule for both editorial Skills: what does a reader **of the language in front of you** do at this passage — take it on one pass, or stop at a word they have to supply. It was built, measured against a matrix frozen before the first run, revised once, measured again, and not shipped. [ADR-0212](../blob/main/docs/adr/0212-a-quotation-is-read-in-the-language-it-is-written-in.md) records the decision; [`docs/evaluation/editorial-363/results.md`](../blob/main/docs/evaluation/editorial-363/results.md) holds the measurement.

The reason it was not shipped is not that the wording was poor. It is that **neither failure reproduced in the Claude family**, so no wording could have been shown to remove one:

- Every source-blind `/redline` run of every arm returned its quoted sentence word for word — the English positive controls, both frozen Swedish inputs, and all three new contrast fixtures. No run expanded a working quotation in any arm, the unchanged product included.
- Both blind judges, in every case, answered that a reader of that text's language takes the passage on one pass. That answer covers *Den tiden skulle jag avsätta innan nästa hus börjar* in the mandatory Swedish control, and it covers *Sedan gick lagret över* in `ellipsis-sv`, the negative control frozen precisely on the premise that a Swedish reader stops there.

## What is left open

**1. The GPT-family failures stay failed.** `docs/evaluation/protocol.md` forbids a Claude session from driving a Codex harness, so they were not retested. The Swedish miss recorded under `docs/evaluation/editorial-329/` and the English over-expansion recorded there are still failures of record. A GPT-family retest is a separate, manual step.

**2. The instrument cannot see the defect, and that is the first thing to settle.** Before another wording is written, there has to be a way to tell whether the defect is present at all. Three of #363's six criteria turned out to have nothing to measure. The sharpest single piece of evidence is `C-ellipsis`: a fixture frozen with an independent criterion, stating that returning *gick lagret över* unchanged and unreported is a miss, against two blind judges who read the passage as ordinary Swedish in all six runs of all three arms. A fixture's criterion is not evidence about a reader, and until that gap is closed an evaluation of this defect measures the judge rather than the product.

**3. Thomas's reading is not overturned by any of this.** Whether *innan nästa hus börjar* is professional Swedish is a judgement about prose. What the measurement establishes is narrower and it is about the instrument.

## What triage might weigh

- Whether a human reading of the frozen Swedish inputs settles the question the judges split from — that is the cheapest way to learn whether there is a defect to chase.
- Whether the judge briefs are the problem: the Redline brief carries an explicit warning that a figure a language uses itself reads on one pass however odd its literal parse, and one judge read the same sentence as one-pass under that brief and as a real hitch under the Write brief. Both readings are in the run tree.
- [#388](https://github.com/Kntnt/skills/issues/388) is the nearest existing piece of the same problem, for `T1` and `R2` rather than for `L1`.

## What is kept and reusable

The three contrast fixtures under [`docs/evaluation/editorial-363/fixtures/`](../blob/main/docs/evaluation/editorial-363/fixtures/), frozen with independent criteria before any product change: one moves the referent and keeps the construction, one moves the language and the rhythm, one is a negative. They exist so that a change cannot pass by learning one sentence, and they are still the right instrument for that.

comments.body:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Triage decision — `ready-for-human`, on both halves

Triage settled this on 2026-09-22. Neither half is work an unattended agent can take, and both are yours.

**1. The GPT-family retest.** `docs/evaluation/protocol.md` forbids a Claude session from driving a Codex harness, so the Swedish miss and the English over-expansion recorded under `docs/evaluation/editorial-329/` stay failures of record and cannot be retested from here. This is the same shape as #362, which is already `ready-for-human` and open for exactly one step — your own Codex retest — and #395, settled the same way today.

**2. The instrument, before any further wording.** The body is right that this is first, and the cheapest way to close it is the one it names: your own reading of the frozen Swedish inputs, which settles whether there is a defect to chase before another evaluation measures the judge instead of the product. `C-ellipsis` is the sharpest case — a fixture frozen on the premise that a Swedish reader stops at *Sedan gick lagret över*, against two blind judges who read it as ordinary Swedish in all six runs of all three arms.

Delegating either half would produce an evaluation of the judges. Nothing is asked of an agent here until one of the two is answered.

**What is kept.** The three contrast fixtures under `docs/evaluation/editorial-363/fixtures/`, frozen with independent criteria before any product change, stay as they are and remain the right instrument for a later attempt. ADR-0212 stands.

---

Settled during triage on 2026-09-22. Written against `682c762b`.

issue.title: The quotation defect #363 was filed on cannot be measured in the Claude family, and stays failed in the GPT family
